text: The semantic layer survives only if it can be understood without you in the room. Three documents close this out: dbt's own docs, exposures that declare dependencies, and a metrics dictionary anyone can read.

Each one does a different job -- dbt docs explains what a model does, exposures show what breaks downstream if it changes, and the metrics dictionary answers the question a non-technical stakeholder actually asks.
Declaring Finance's dashboard as an exposure puts it directly on the lineage graph -- anyone about to change int_active_members sees the blast radius before they merge, not after something breaks.
Active Member, defined in plain language, with what it excludes spelled out, owned by analytics engineering, changeable only with sign-off from the three teams who adopted it.
The system is documented well enough to outlive this project. Last video: an honest look at what this build actually changed, and what's still manual.
